title: Rates, policy expectations, releases and calendar context at the 05:00 London cutoff

assigned_to.note: A second frontier model, given the same contract but a disjoint card set, so A1 and A2 do not see each other's drafts.

target_contract.endpoint: 05:00 Europe/London on the next local date (05:00Z GMT, 04:00Z BST); one 24-hour London-to-London session
target_contract.label: sign of the label-instrument change from cutoff to endpoint, flat band frozen separately

coordinator_context_allowed: Inventory of the deployed engine: docs/research/usd-session/v1/inventory.md
The deployed engine's own rulebook, as live input: logic/agent_usd_direction.md
Reachable data (read-only): the FRED series named in data/usd-24h-dataset-manifest.json, and the repository's economic-calendar artefacts if any are reachable
coordinator_analysis_withheld: No expected sign or size is supplied, and no finding from the closed 24-hour study is sent with this assignment.
cards_to_produce: rates.us-front-end-delta (2Y and 3M yield changes as policy-expectation proxies)
rates.relative-front-end-delta (US versus Germany and versus other G10 front ends, with the euro-area and UK legs named)
rates.real-yield-delta (10Y and 5Y real yields, and the breakeven split)
rates.term-premium-and-curve (10Y minus 2Y, and whether the level or the change matters)
rates.credit-spread-delta (high-yield spread change as a risk and growth proxy)
calendar.known-releases-between-cutoff-and-endpoint (which releases are scheduled inside the window and how a known-but-unreleased event may be used without using its outcome)
macro.release-surprise-at-first-print (including the honest answer if consensus vintages are unavailable)
questions_every_card_must_answer: Which yields or spreads are genuinely observable at 05:00 London today, and with what publication lag?
Which part of a release is a reaction that is already in the price by the cutoff and which part is still predictive?
How do these cards overlap with each other and with the price-behaviour cards, and what would be double-counted?
What would have to be true for the relation to change sign inside a London-to-London 24-hour session?
What is the programmable hypothesis, the allowed parameters, and the result that kills it?

deliverable.format: one JSON file per card following docs/research/usd-session/v1/research-card.schema.json

rules: A scheduled release may enter as a known calendar event; its outcome may not, unless a first-print value genuinely existed before the cutoff.
State clearly when a required vintage or consensus series is unavailable, and mark the card accordingly rather than proxying silently.
Do not carry over any USD-specific sign, weight or threshold to another asset; other assets are out of scope.
No production, workflow, dashboard or configuration change is authorised by this assignment.
